When you re‑import a corrected file, Meridian’s importer will match existing contacts by email (or by the unique ID you include) and update the matching record instead of creating a duplicate – as long as the field used for matching wasn’t the one you changed. If you corrected the email address or the identifier itself, the importer can’t recognise the row as the same record, so the safest approach is to remove the rows that already succeeded from the file before you run the import again. Alternatively, you can re‑run the import with only the rows that need fixing. arguments.message: Hi there! When you re‑import a corrected file, Meridian’s importer will match existing contacts by email (or by the unique ID you include) and update the matching record instead of creating a duplicate – as long as the field used for matching wasn’t the one you changed. If you corrected the email address or the identifier itself, the importer can’t recognise the row as the same record, so the safest approach is to remove the rows that already succeeded from the file before you run the import again. Alternatively, you can re‑run the import with only the rows that need fixing. This will prevent duplicate records from being created.
